title: Transient kernel-hung threads and KV-cache loss — oncall diary
content:
Summary:
A recurring class of incidents observed on inference hosts where a subset of worker processes report corrupted or missing KV-cache entries after a transient kernel-thread hang on the node. Symptoms started 2026-06-02 00:40 UTC during a mid-night batch window: increased tail latency on chat endpoints, followed by client-visible hallucinations (repeats / truncated responses).

Why this doc:
- Capture noisy signals we saw on-call and correlate kernel-side hangs to application-level KV-cache loss.
- Record quick mitigation that bought us time and list follow-ups for the runtime and node teams.

Observed symptoms (live):
- Two GPUs on node gpu-node-08 reported nv_peer_errors ~ 0 (no obvious NVLink tear), but driver logs show multiple "hung task" kernel traces.
- Several serving processes (runtimes) reported KV-cache mismatch errors in logs: "kvcache: missing token keys for prefix N" and subsequent truncated generation.
- Node-level: high ksoftirqd CPU for a short window (~30s), then kernel watchdog triggered a GPU reset for the processes on that GPU.
- Clients saw 502s for a small percentage and malformed outputs for ~120s total.

Timeline (approx):
- 00:40:03 UTC: first alert — route p99 latency breach, tracing shows stall at prefix lookup.
- 00:40:12 UTC: ops channel — oncall picks up, begin tailing /var/log/messages and dmesg.
- 00:40:21 UTC: dmesg snippet: "INFO: task kworker/3:2:4298 blocked for more than 120 seconds."
- 00:40:29 UTC: runtime logs: "kvcache: lookup TX_482 missing key 0x7f9a...\n  fallback to full decode" (multiple instances).
- 00:41:10 UTC: GPU reset recorded (nvidia-smi shows lockups), processes restarted by systemd unit and reclaimed.
- 00:42:10 UTC: partial service recovery; some clients still report truncated outputs.
- 00:44:00 UTC: p99 back to normal but we kept a small elevated error rate until manual drain and canary rollout.

Initial triage notes:
- Not pure ECC storm: ECC counters are near baseline, no large correctable error spike.
- NVLink counters show periodic retransmits but not sustained flap.
- Kernel traces show many tasks stuck in __schedule(), waiting on a futex inside the driver stack — suggests driver callpath entering uninterruptible sleep.
- kworker stuck + high ksoftirqd suggests an interrupt storm or ring buffer backlog that temporarily starved kernel threads.

Relevant log excerpts (sanitized):
- dmesg:
  "[Jun  2 00:40:21] INFO: task kworker/3:2:4298 blocked for more than 120 seconds.\n [Jun  2 00:40:21] Tracing blocked tasks:\n\tCall Trace:\n\t __schedule+0x2a7/0x6d0\n\t schedule+0x45/0xb0\n\t driver_lock_wait+0x1f\n  "

- runtime log (serving-runtime-1):
  "2026-06-02T00:40:29Z WARN kvcache_lookup: missing keys for request=tx_482 prefix_len=64\n fallback=decode_entire_context\n  "

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- We drained the affected GPU (evacuated pods/containers) using the node-drain script to stop churn. That reduced client-visible errors quickly.
- Tuned systemd restart backoff to avoid thundering restarts of the serving process (temporarily increased RestartSec from 5s to 20s for the runtime unit).
- Temporarily switched route p95 traffic to node group "dedicated-slow-fallover" while we held the node for postmortem.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver path enters a rare state where an interrupt ring/buffer is saturated (RX/TX queues), causing kworker to block in wait and the driver to fail to marshal async KV-cache updates to userland => user processes see missing keys.
2) A kernel preemption issue combined with a long-running softirq loop starves the runtime threads responsible for flushing KV updates, causing them to lose synchronization and mark entries stale.
3) Subtle memory corruption triggered by a GPU reset race (rare), leading to in-process KV-cache index mismatches (less likely given no ECC spike).

Quick repro attempt notes (lab):
- Attempted synthetic load: continuous small-token generations with randomized prefixes plus a 1MB/s cross-GPU memcpy to exercise NVLink. After ~30m on the lab rig, observed elevated ksoftirqd but could not reproduce kernel hang deterministically.
- Instrumented runtime to log KV-cache enqueue/dequeue counts — saw bursts of enqueue failures aligned with increased softirq.

Monitoring queries and dashboards to add (short):
- Add KV-cache miss rate per process / host (new metric: runtime.kvcache.miss_ratio).
- Alert if (kworker_blocked_seconds > 60 && runtime.kvcache.miss_ratio > 0.01) for any node.
- Dashboard panel showing ksoftirqd CPU + softnet backlog + driver RX ring utilization.

Short-term action items (owner / ETA):
- (Oliver) Add kvcache.miss_ratio metric and an experimental alert — 48h.
- (Priya) Add tracepoints in serving-runtime around KV enqueue/dequeue (lightweight) and ship to prod on a small canary group — 72h.
- (Diego) Coordinate with kernel/driver team to get a debug-enabled driver build that logs ring head/tail pointers during the spike window for one canary rack — 1 week.

Longer-term work (investigation threads):
- Root-cause verification with debug driver logs; correlate ring pointer wrap and kworker block windows.
- Evaluate adding a userland watchdog in the runtime: if KV enqueue latency > X ms for Y seconds, flush/serialize context to avoid silent loss.
- Consider driver-level quota/throttle on interrupts or move heavy bookkeeping off softirq to a dedicated kernel thread to reduce starvation risk.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did the issue affect KV-cache write-path and not general GPU compute? (partial answer: KV writes are async and depend on timely RX/TX completion; compute can be restarted after reset which hides some failure modes)
- Are certain model sizes / prefix-length distributions more likely to hit this (we saw more cases on long-context chat workloads)?
- Could recent runtime changes (PR 892) that batch KV writes be exposing a lock contention bug?

Notes to postmortem (for later):
- Collect full systemd coredumps and link to JIRA-3157.
- Keep the affected node quarantined for driver debug build (don't repro image-swap in the wild).

Loose checklist for next oncall if this recurs:
- 1) Isolate node, collect dmesg + driver ring counters, snapshot /proc/interrupts.
- 2) Evacuate GPU workloads; do not allow automated restarts until driver logs collected.
- 3) If KV-cache misses present, manually route traffic off node group and enable canary fallback.

Closing thought:
This felt different from classic ECC or NVLink link-failure incidents — the signature was a short kernel-thread starvation window with a cascade into the userland KV paths. Prioritize low-overhead observability around KV enqueue timings and driver ring utilization before we attempt heavier kernel patches.

TODO (small):
- Attach the full dmesg export + runtime logs to JIRA-3157 (Maya) — by 2026-06-04.
- Run the synthetic repro for 24h on a driver-debug node and report results (Diego) — by 2026-06-09.
- Draft a minimal userland watchdog proposal for runtime (Priya) — by 2026-06-10.

-- end of diary entry (initial)
